body:
A Claude-family evaluation made from a Claude Code session cannot judge two criteria of `docs/evaluation/corpus/editorial-quality/README.md`, because a subagent's transcript is not readable from the session that started it:

- **T1** — "resolved configuration **and actual loaded files**".
- **R2** — what "the trace establish[es]": full scoped contract loading, a fresh correction agent, and exactly one closing installed Proofread pass with no substantive edit after it.

Both are recorded `skipped` on every entry of the #386 records (`write-claude-2026-09-21-386.md`, `redline-claude-2026-09-21-386.md`), and #380's readiness addendum prescribes the same for its records and asks for this issue. So in this family nothing yet says whether Write loads only its bounded contract or whether Redline's closing Proofread pass ran.

What is asked for: a way to run one staged Skill invocation in the Claude family and keep its full trace — every file read, every command, every subagent started with its prompt — where an evaluator can read it afterwards, under the protocol's provider-isolation rule. It is a method limit and no defect of either Skill.

Named by #386 and #380.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

Thomas approved this scope on 2026-09-21. This comment is the requirement wherever it amends the body; otherwise the body stands. Read the whole thread before building.

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Capture an evaluator-readable trace of one staged Claude-family Skill invocation, including its nested agents, so T1 and R2 can be judged.

### What to build

The #386 records skip T1 and R2 because their evaluator could not inspect the run agents' transcripts. That is a limit of that evaluation method, not evidence that Claude never persists such transcripts. Repository inspection found native transcript readers in Model Selector's capture machinery, including the distinction between a parent transcript and a stopped subagent's own transcript. Those readers are groundwork, not an existing solution: Model Selector deliberately does not retain transcript contents in Measurements. The existing native evaluation runner captures GPT-family runs.

Provide a repeatable Claude-native evaluation entry point for one staged Skill invocation. Preserve the exact Formal Invocation and Contextual Instruction, staged instruction and corpus revisions, resolved Harness/model identity and exposed deliberation, completion status, response, and before-and-after inventories. Retain the parent transcript and every nested agent transcript belonging to that invocation, with enough parent/child identity and ordering to reconstruct who ran what. Preserve the recorded prompts, tool calls, arguments and results needed to establish file/scope loading, commands, corrections and the closing installed Proofread pass. Distinguish actual recorded activity from what a run says it did; a path mentioned in prose is not proof that it was read.

Reuse existing staging, transcript discovery and cleanup mechanisms where appropriate. Keep evaluation evidence separate from Model Selector's Measurement store and outside the run's disposable scratch. Record missing, truncated or inaccessible trace segments explicitly: never present an incomplete trace as complete or infer a pass from the run's self-report. Account for shell-mediated reads at the level the native trace actually exposes, documenting any remaining observability limit.

The runner must terminate and clean up its own process group and scratch on success, failure, timeout and interruption, while retaining the evidence and status needed to understand an incomplete run.

### Key interfaces

- The staged invocation entry point: one Skill invocation in one provider-native run.
- Native parent/child transcript identities and captured tool activity.
- The evaluation protocol's T1/R2 evidence and record fields; no scoring criteria are weakened.
- Existing native transcript readers may inform implementation; the Measurement contract does not change.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A documented entry point produces a self-contained evidence packet for one staged invocation, with exact invocation material, identities, revisions, response, inventories and completion status.
- [ ] A real Claude-native Write run with a source checker and a real Claude-native Redline run exercising a fresh correction and its closing installed Proofread pass retain the nested traces needed for an independent evaluator to assign T1 and R2 pass or fail with cited evidence. The Skill need not pass those criteria; the method must make them observable.
- [ ] The evidence establishes what was loaded and the order of correction, re-review and final Proofread, including whether any substantive edit followed it.
- [ ] Missing-child, truncated-trace and interrupted-run checks demonstrate explicit incomplete status and retention of available evidence; no successful completeness claim is inferred from a summary.
- [ ] Cleanup checks show no run-owned process survives and no unrelated process or file is removed.
- [ ] Provider isolation holds: Claude-native validation is performed in a Claude session. A Codex session may prepare code or inspect saved evidence but must not invoke or control Claude to validate it, and must not claim completion without the required native validation.
- [ ] Existing records remain historical; new validation evidence and any protocol records are indexed under their applicable conventions.
- [ ] The four checks in CONTRIBUTING.md pass; regenerate the Catalog if any shipped file changes.

### Out of scope

Changing Write or Redline's editorial behavior; weakening T1/R2; cross-provider orchestration; adding transcript contents to Measurements; retroactively turning earlier skipped criteria into passes.

### Blocked by

No prerequisite ticket. #380 and #386 supplied the method-limit evidence; this work does not depend on rerunning either whole evaluation.

## Readiness addendum

This comment amends the execution assignment in the Agent Brief. Its implementation scope and acceptance criteria remain in force.

### What to build

**Execution constraint: assign this entire ticket to a Claude-native session with a working Claude Harness and access to its native transcripts.** That session owns both implementation and the required real Claude-native validation. Check those capabilities before starting the build. Do not dispatch this ticket to a Codex builder for unattended completion.

The earlier sentence “A Codex session may prepare code or inspect saved evidence” permits preparatory work only; it does not define a split execution plan or a validation handoff. This ticket has no cross-provider handoff. A Codex session may inspect it, but must leave the implementation task for a separately started Claude-native session and must not start, control or invoke that session. The provider-isolation rule in `docs/evaluation/protocol.md` remains unchanged.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The owning build and validation session is Claude-native and can perform the required runs without a cross-provider handoff.
- [ ] Implementation alone, synthetic trace tests or inspection from Codex do not complete this ticket; the real native validation and all existing acceptance criteria remain required.

This resolves the readiness stop on “Claude-native validation is performed in a Claude session”: the validation owner is the same Claude-native session that owns the build, not an unspecified later operator.

## Triage — the work is delivered; what remains is yours

Re-read on 2026-09-23. **This ticket is no longer work for an agent, and its `ready-for-agent` label was actively dangerous**: an unattended run would have rebuilt what is already built. Moved to `ready-for-human`.

The trace-bearing harness was implemented on the branch `codex/orchestrate-388-391`, in the commits that introduce the native-trace capture and the segment-by-segment command judging, together with `docs/evaluation/editorial-388/`. That branch also carries #383's delivery and #390's and #391's, is eleven commits ahead of `main`, and is behind it by three.

**What remains is the merge**, and it is yours rather than an agent's: `main` is being worked by another session, and the merge is being held back deliberately rather than disturb it.

**Why this ticket is worth watching rather than just closing.** Eleven open tickets are blocked on that merge — #385, #387, #389, #394, #397, #398, #399, #400, #401, #402, #403, #404 and #415 name it, most of them pointing at this number as the readable edge, because #383 is closed and no longer reads as a blocker. Closing this one before the merge would remove the only open ticket those edges can point at.

**After the merge:** close this, and the blocked-by notes on the others fall away. #396, #414 and #416 are buildable without it.
